name: Deng Xiaoping Theory
summary: Deng Xiaoping Theory is the Chinese Communist Party's guiding doctrine of the reform era. It keeps one-party rule, public ownership as the mainstay and Marxism-Leninism-Mao Zedong Thought as binding principles, while judging policy by whether it develops the productive forces. It accepts markets, foreign capital and some people getting rich first as tools of socialism, prefers gradual and stable change, and rejects Western-style democracy and separation of powers.
scope: The doctrine as set out in Deng's own speeches, 1978-1992 (Four Cardinal Principles, political reform, one country two systems, Southern Tour), as written into the Party and state constitutions that name it, and as the reform-era record shows it. Excludes later additions by Jiang, Hu and Xi, and Mao-era positions Deng repudiated.

missingStatements.text: A country may let some regions and people get rich first so that others follow.
missingStatements.rationale: Deng said some regions should develop first and later help poorer ones, warning against polarisation.

missingStatements.text: Markets and economic planning are both only tools, and neither defines a social system.
missingStatements.rationale: Deng stated that a planned economy is not socialism because capitalism also has planning, and that markets exist under socialism.

missingStatements.text: Officials should be limited to fixed terms and retire, with no one holding office for life.
missingStatements.rationale: Deng said no leading cadre should hold any office indefinitely.

missingStatements.text: Open, foreign-invested special economic zones can serve a country's development without abandoning its political system.
missingStatements.rationale: Deng defended the special zones and foreign firms as useful supplements while public ownership remains the mainstay.
missingStatements.declined: Special economic zones are specific to China; free-trade and delink-world-market cover the openness axis.

notes: Answers follow what Deng's speeches, the Party and state constitutions and the Britannica record state; statements none of them address are null. Practice under later leaders (Jiang, Xi) can differ from Deng's own texts.

keyFigures.role: Architect of China's reform and opening; the Party constitution names the theory after him
keyFigures.quote: thus founding Deng Xiaoping Theory. Deng Xiaoping Theory is the outcome of the integration of the basic tenets of Marxism-Leninism

central-planning.rationale: Deng (1992): "A planned economy is not equivalent to socialism, because there is planning under capitalism too", and planning and market forces "are both means"; he gave planning no superiority over the market.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Deng (1979): the remaining hostile elements are "a special form of the leftover, under socialist conditions, of the class struggles of past history", though he was "opposed to broadening the scope of class struggle".

death-penalty.rationale: Deng (1983): murderers, robbers and gang members "should be arrested and prosecuted without fail, reformed through labour or severely punished according to law. A number of criminals should be executed according to law".

delink-world-market.rationale: Deng (1992) said development must include "an export-oriented economy" and, in 1985, that China would "absorb foreign capital and introduce advanced technology".

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Deng (1979): "we must uphold the dictatorship of the proletariat" as a second cardinal principle, since socialism "cannot be defended or built up without" it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Deng (1987): "At present, indirect elections are held for posts above the county level, and direct elections are held for those at the county level and below", and general elections on the mainland could come only "sometime in the next century".

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Deng (1989): "we had to quell the turmoil by imposing martial law. If factors that might cause unrest emerge in future, we shall take tough measures to eliminate them as quickly as possible".

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Deng (1984) described China's foreign policy as "independent and truly non-aligned", refusing to side with either superpower.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Deng (1979) said "We must do away with equalitarianism and the practice of “sharing food from the same big pot”", while in 1985 he said socialism aims at prosperity for all and not polarization, so he rejects levelling but wants common prosperity.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Deng (1987) described China as a state with "dozens of minority nationalities" among the Han majority, and said policy rests on "genuine equality of the nationalities" and on developing the minority areas.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Deng (1984), on reunification with Taiwan: "if the problem cannot be solved by peaceful means, then it must be solved by force".

gradual-change.rationale: Deng (1985): "we began our reform step by step, starting with the countryside".

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Deng (1978) defended distribution according to work as the socialist principle and rejected distribution by politics or seniority; his 1985 text also allows a small private sector, so ownership income is not excluded altogether.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Deng (1990): "It won't work to require all the countries in the world to copy the patterns set by the United States, Britain and France. There are many Islamic countries ... In these countries it is absolutely impossible to introduce a so-called democratic system of the American type." In 1987 he said Hong Kong's system need not be a total copy of the British or American one.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Deng (1990): "The key principle governing the new international order should be noninterference in other countries' internal affairs and social systems."

leader-cult.rationale: Deng (1980) listed "practising the cult of personality and placing individuals above the organization" among the Party's major problems and said commemoration of leaders sometimes "smacked of the cult of personality".

limit-population.rationale: Deng (1979): "We must greatly increase our efforts in family planning", since a large population creates serious problems "with regard to food, education and employment".

majority-settlement.rationale: Deng (1987), on Tibet: "there is no harm in having some Han people go there to help", and where Han numbers are large and helping local people develop the economy, "that's not a bad thing".

market-under-party-rule.rationale: In the 1992 southern tour Deng said "A planned economy is not equivalent to socialism... a market economy is not capitalism, because there are markets under socialism too"; the 1979 speech makes upholding "the leadership of the Communist Party" one of four cardinal principles.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Deng (1980) said the revised system must "enable the areas inhabited by minority nationalities to exercise genuine regional autonomy".

moral-incentives.rationale: Deng (1978) insisted that distribution be "according to a person's work, not according to his politics or his seniority", and in 1979 said pay must reward outstanding work, so duty alone does not replace material reward.

nation-first.rationale: Deng (1989): "We are more keenly aware that first priority should always be given to national sovereignty and security."

one-party-rule.rationale: Deng (1979) made it a cardinal principle: "we must uphold the leadership of the Communist Party", saying the proletariat's survival is impossible without its political party.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Party constitution: "The Communist Party of China persists in its leadership over the People's Liberation Army and other people's armed forces".

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Party constitution (Article 1) requires members to be "willing to ... carry out the Party's decisions".

pay-for-effort.rationale: Deng (1978) argued for the socialist principle of "to each according to his work": "distribution should be made only according to a person's work".

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Deng (1989) said "first priority should always be given to national sovereignty and security" and asked of foreign pressure: "What grounds have they for interfering in the internal affairs of China? Who gave them power to do that?"

public-ownership.rationale: Deng (1985): "predominance of public ownership and common prosperity are the two fundamental socialist principles that we must adhere to"; "its economy must be dominated by public ownership".

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Deng (1987): "In the People's Republic of China there is no discrimination against different nationalities, and our policy in Tibet is based on genuine equality of the nationalities."

region-keeps-system.rationale: Deng (1984): "within the People’s Republic of China, the mainland with its one billion people will maintain the socialist system, while Hong Kong and Taiwan continue under the capitalist system", with Hong Kong's policies unchanged for 50 years.

religious-nation.rationale: Deng (1979) spoke of "China's patriots, whatever their nationality and religion", as one united body building socialism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Deng (1992): "The chief criterion for making that judgement should be whether it promotes the growth of the productive forces in a socialist society, increases the overall strength of the socialist state and raises living standards".

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Deng (1984): "Reunification of the motherland is the aspiration of the whole nation. If it cannot be accomplished in 100 years, it will be in 1,000 years."

rich-first.rationale: Deng (1985): "In encouraging some regions to become prosperous first, we intend that they should inspire others to follow their example and that all of them should help economically backward regions to develop", with the aim being all-round prosperity rather than polarization.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Deng (1980) criticised "letting only one person have the say" and the cult of personality, and the Central Committee ordered "less publicity for individuals".

separated-powers.rationale: Deng (1987), on Hong Kong: it would not be appropriate "for its system to be a total copy of theirs with, for example, the separation of the three powers".

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Deng (1978): "Very often, what leaders say is taken as the law and anyone who disagrees is called a law-breaker" and said democracy "has to be institutionalized and written into law" so it does not change with the leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: Deng (1979): "so long as class struggle exists and so long as imperialism and hegemonism exist, it is inconceivable that the dictatorial function of the state should wither away".

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Deng (1984): "China’s foreign policy is independent and truly non-aligned. We will not play the “United States card” or the “Soviet Union card”."

suppress-opposition.rationale: Deng (1989): "They support the resolute action taken against the rebellion" and "we should quell the rebellion completely. This is a fine opportunity to dismantle all the illegal organizations in China".

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Deng (1980) named "life tenure in leading posts" among the major problems of Party and state and called for regular retirement of cadres.

vanguard-party.rationale: Deng (1979) said the survival of the movement "is impossible without the political parties of the proletariat", and in 1985 called for lofty ideals and "a strong sense of discipline" in the Party's ranks.
